key_insight: By concatenating GKP and Steane error-correcting codes, the paper shows that an all-photonic repeater can support 1,000 km communication with only 9 km spacing while staying resource-efficient.
engineering_relevance: This lowers the photonic resource burden for practical quantum networks by combining loss tolerance, optical memory modeling, and realistic imperfection-aware protocol design.
method: Use concatenated bosonic GKP and discrete-variable [[7,1,3]] Steane codes to protect Bell pairs against photon loss.
Add a multi-reflection mirror-based free-space optical cavity as a photonic memory model and rank candidate constructions with a new criterion.
Compare two heuristic Bell-pair construction strategies: one uses more GKP qubits with up to 2-qubit correlated errors, the other uses fewer GKP qubits with up to 3-qubit correlated errors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulations including switching-induced and standard optical imperfections, with the proposed setup requiring only a few thousand GKP qubits per repeater station per run.
watch_item: The architecture’s practicality depends on achieving the assumed optical-cavity, switching, and mirror-efficiency performance in a real experimental setting.
paper_title: High-Rate and Resource-Efficient All-Photonic Quantum Repeater Architectures with 9 km Repeater Spacing
